applied.fact: Summit time holds the car-to-car total

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Tonasket, cross the Okanogan River and drive west on Loomis-Oroville Road to Loomis.

sectionBreakdown.note: Nearly all parties do this route car-to-car in one long day: climb out of Long Swamp Campground through old burn to Two Bear Camp for water, then continue up open, formerly-timbere…
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Long Swamp Trail to the summit and back

access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass (or Interagency/America the Beautiful pass) required for trailhead parking, or $5/vehicle/day self-pay if no pass; Senior, Access, and Military passes are exempt from the day-use fee.
access.rules: Standard Pasayten Wilderness regulations apply (group-size limits, no mechanized/motorized travel, Leave No Trace, pack out all trash); certified weed-free hay/pellets are required for any pack or saddle stock. Dogs allowed on leash.
access.permit: Free self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead register (Pasayten Wilderness).
access.closures: Trail is typically snowbound until roughly June/early July; check Methow Valley Ranger District conditions before an early-season trip. High fire-danger closures are possible in late summer — verify current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts before driving in.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — the Long Swamp/Windy Peak Trail #342 corridor and trailhead fall within this district's Pasayten Wilderness portion, not the neighboring Tonasket Ranger District.
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or equivalent Interagency pass.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead registration box. No reservation is needed.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Full-day fitness for a long trail outing - on the order of 10-14 miles round trip with sustained elevation gain via the Windy Creek or Long Swamp approach; needs to hold a steady pace over many hours
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Day-hike weight (roughly 15-20 lb including extra water, since the upper route has limited water, plus layers and lightning-storm contingency gear); overnight car-camp option at Long Swamp adds standard backpacking weight for that leg only

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long access drive (20+ miles of paved/gravel Toats Coulee Road to the Long Swamp / Windy Peak trail system) plus a several-mile trail approach one-way to the summit, making this a full long day or a car-camp-and-day-hike trip
requiredSkills: Trail navigation over a long, remote approach
Basic mountain-weather judgment - willingness to retreat off the exposed summit ridge if thunderstorms build
Self-sufficiency for a remote wilderness trailhead (long drive-in, no cell coverage, limited water high on the route)
No technical or scrambling skills required - standard maintained-trail walk-up
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Beginner-to-intermediate hiker is fine technically (Class 1 maintained trail, no exposure or scrambling skill needed), but a partner should be comfortable with long, remote, self-sufficient wilderness days - this is noted as the farthest Bulger from any trailhead, reached via a long paved/gravel access road with no cell coverage

weather.typical: Typical dry Pasayten/Okanogan summer-to-fall pattern - warm, dry midsummer days giving way to cooler, more unsettled weather by September-October
weather.probability: Afternoon thunderstorms are the primary named risk (lightning on the exposed summit); most likely July-August

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Low fall-exposure overall (Class 1 maintained trail), but an exposed summit ridge carries real lightning/weather exposure - the main consequence risk is being caught high and exposed in a thunderstorm, not a fall

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July through October, with the most reliable conditions in July and August

July.reason: Start of the best-season window; snow largely melted off the trail and summit ridge with long daylight for the long mileage

June.reason: Outside the season window; lingering snow at elevation and potentially wet/rutted access road are likely, though not confirmed

August.reason: Peak of the best-season window; driest, most stable trail and road conditions, but watch for the afternoon lightning risk already flagged on the exposed summit

October.reason: Tail end of best season; early snow, freezing temps, and possible road conditions on the long gravel approach become more likely

September.reason: Still within best season; cooler temps and fewer bugs, generally stable, but shorter daylight for the long round trip
